result:
Round 10 is done, but only the ruler bug is fixed. The late-video-after-loop bug (C-R7-01) had no fixable cause in the app, so I changed no source for it, and it will most likely still fail C's check (R10-W1). The full report is at `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-10.md`. Nothing was committed or pushed, and I'm not claiming any acceptance ID as passed.

**C-R7-01 (video lands late after a loop wrap):** I added temporary logging to the video dock and ran 6 runs ├ù 3 wraps on the L6 layout (two of them straight after a fresh page load). The logging is removed and the dock is byte-identical to its start-of-round copy. In my runs 9 of 18 wraps landed below 2.29.
- **(a) late pre-seek: ruled out.** The standby seek starts about 1 s before the wrap and settles about 0.91ΓÇô0.96 s before it.
- **(b) first-swap warm-up: ruled out.** `play()` ΓåÆ `playing` takes 4.5ΓÇô7.7 ms on every swap, with no outlier on the first one.
- **(d) standby accepted behind its target: ruled out.** The standby is exactly on its target (offset 0.000) at all 18 swaps.
- **(m) measurement only: ruled out.** The video really lags: up to 0.044ΓÇô0.055 s, and ΓêÆ0.014 to ΓêÆ0.024 s at +300 ms.
- **What the data supports is (c), the environment.** On every swap, about 22ΓÇô51 ms after `play()`, the video's `currentTime` stalls even though the app does nothing (rate 1, no seek). The sync loop then catches up, but the D-19 design stops correcting once the error is within 0.02 s. So the landing settles about 0.02 s late, outside the ┬▒0.01 window of the RF5-2 check.
- **That is a conflict between two specs, which B or the Tech Lead must decide.** I changed neither. Steady-state error in these runs is already about 0.010ΓÇô0.013 s.
- **Harness note for C:** the +300 ms sample falls at either 0.302 or 0.310 s depending on run phase, and is always compared to a fixed 2.30. The same 0.02 s lag can therefore read 2.276 or 2.292.
- **None of the allowed fixes reaches the stall.** Pre-rolling the standby would need both videos playing for more than one frame, which the 17 ms limit forbids. Starting `play()` one frame early would just be tuning to these runs.
- **R10-W3 (unit test of a fix) doesn't apply**, because there is no fix.

**C-R7-02 (ruler overflows by 1.41ΓÇô1.47 px):** the cause is the last ruler tick, sitting exactly at the content's right edge. Its 1 px line sticks out by one pixel, and Chrome rounds `scrollWidth`.
- **Fix:** `rulerTickMarks` in `app/lib/arrangement/view.ts` now drops any tick whose line would pass the ruler end, using a new constant `RULER_TICK_LINE_PX = 1`. No tick that carries a label can be dropped.
- **Visible change:** there's no longer a thin line at the very end of the timeline, which sits inside the 30 s empty tail. This is noted in doc 019.
- **My measurement after the fix:** maximum overflow is 0.5 px at 1280├ù720 and 0.484 px at 1440├ù900, and 0 on the empty default. Label counts at every zoom match C's round-7 sweep. My script doesn't count overlapping or cut labels; C's sweep does.
- **Tests:** three new cases in `view.test.ts` use C's two worst zooms plus the empty default. They fail on the old function and pass now; the proof is in `a-round-10/guard-c-r7-02.txt`.
- **One existing expectation changed** for an empty 30 s timeline: 31 ticks become 30, and the last tick is now `{29, '0:29'}` instead of `{30, null}`.

**Files changed:** `view.ts`, `view.test.ts`, doc 018 (status and TODO lines only), and the new doc `019-studio-lab-round10-wrap-ruler.md`.
- The 15 frozen files and the 4 protected files are unchanged.
- `Header.tsx` is identical to HEAD.

**Checks:**
- **Tests:** 812/812 pass on the final full run. The run before it had one 5 s timeout in `sfx-library.test.tsx`, a file I didn't touch. It passed alone and in the re-run, so it looks load-sensitive.
